title: In UK Budget, No News Is Good News
text:
In UK Budget, No News Is Good News

Anatole Kaletsky

Gavekal Research | 30 Oct 2026

Sometimes a non-event is a great event. This can obviously be true in geopolitics, when a war or terrorist attack is avoided. But it can also apply to economic policy. A good example is Britain’s annual budget charade, which inflicts on the country a curse of fiscal fundamentalism unknown in any other mature democracy by twinning the crazy tradition of “budget secrecy,” which turns any discussion of fiscal plans into a crime worse than treason, with the even crazier convention of “parliamentary confidence,” which demands immediate resignation of any government that loses a budget vote.Between them, these two absurdities of Britain’s “unwritten constitution” exempt tax legislation from the rational debate and technocratic scrutiny taken for granted before any new legislation on infinitely less consequential issues like the regulation of bus routes or the protection of newts.
